title: Contact points and consent have no named operation in the rwb-source-data contract
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Party and Customer Master Data Design v3.xlsx
section: Party fields (v_ace_contact 9 rows, contact_point_ext 7 rows); Read paths
description: v3 reads contact points from v_ace_contact and keeps consent, verification and failed attempts in contact_point_ext, and rwb-comms needs a contact point to send a notice. Under the realignment only rwb-source-data may read the views (DP-05), and its contract lists GET /customers/{id}, /accounts/{id}, GET /collateral/{id}, /payments?accountId=, GET /freshness and POST /business-days/{date}/ready. None of them names contacts or consent, so 16 of the 52 field rows have no stated read operation.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 15 line 1114 (rwb-source-data IN: GET /customers/{id}, /accounts/{id}; GET /collateral/{id}, /payments?accountId=; GET /freshness; POST /business-days/{date}/ready) and line 1115 (OUT); slide 41 line 2884 (P1 owns the ACE view contract); slide 17 line 1210 (rwb-comms IN: POST /notices, GET /cases/{id}/notices, no contact read); slide 45 line 3038 (only rwb-source-data reads the 30 views); v3 Party fields rows 31 to 39 and 45 to 51.
area: Data / party and contact read contract
proposed: Add the contact read to the rwb-source-data customer contract (either GET /customers/{id}/contacts or contact points inside the customer payload) in the P1 CON story, and cite that operation in this sheet's Read paths.

title: No write operation is defined for party_ext and contact_point_ext under the single-writer rule
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Party and Customer Master Data Design v3.xlsx
section: Party fields (party_ext 5 rows, contact_point_ext 7 rows); Match rules
description: v3 has the Workbench write the party flags and the contact consent, verification and failure counters. With one writer per schema (DP-01) those writes belong to rwb-source-data, but the Arch v5 contract shows only reads plus POST /business-days/{date}/ready for P1, so the services that set a flag (deviation screening for deceased and bankruptcy, comms for consent and failed_count) have no command to call.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 15 line 1114 and line 1115 (the P1 IN list has no command except the business-day POST); slide 41 line 2884; slide 29 line 2149 (each service writes only its own schema, no cross-schema writes); slide 15 line 1111 (rwb-deviation OUT: REST Source data: party flags, read only); v3 Party fields rows 24 to 30 and 45 to 51.
proposed: Define P1 command operations for the party flags and for contact consent and verification in the P1 CON story, and state in this sheet that no other service writes rwb_source_data.

title: v_ace_ca_relation has no named consumer or operation in Architecture v5
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Party and Customer Master Data Design v3.xlsx
description: The guarantor and co-borrower relation is read from v_ace_ca_relation in v3. In the 19-service design the only candidate operation is GET /accounts/{id} on rwb-source-data, and no service is named as its consumer: the guarantee contract lists no source-data read, and the valuation contract reads collateral and appraisals only.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 15 line 1114 (GET /accounts/{id}); slide 18 line 1348 (rwb-guarantee contract, no source-data read); slide 18 line 1341 (rwb-valuation reads collateral and appraisals); slide 41 line 2884; v3 Party fields rows 40 to 44.
proposed: State that v_ace_ca_relation is served by GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/accounts/{id} and name the route services that read it in the P1 CON and the S3 CON stories.

title: The match-rule narrative still assumes a customer row lands in the Workbench
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Party and Customer Master Data Design v3.xlsx
section: Match rules (row 2 and the merged note in row 11)
description: v3 says M1 to M4 run in ACE ingestion before a customer row reaches the Workbench and that the Workbench reads one person_key. Architecture v5 lands no customer row in a Recovery schema: rwb-source-data reads recovery.v_ace_customer at query time and publishes AceDataReady. The sentence is therefore outdated, although it is preserved word for word in v4.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 line 2884 (P1 owns the ACE view contract, extension tables, freshness, reconciliation); slide 37 line 2679 (views read only by rwb-source-data); slide 43 line 2952 (AceDataReady producer rwb-source-data); v3 Match rules row 2 and row 11.
proposed: Read every 'reaches the Workbench' phrase as 'is served by rwb-source-data', and correct the wording at the next content review rather than in the realignment copy.

title: The masking function and the masking policy have no stated home after the schema split
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Party and Customer Master Data Design v3.xlsx
description: v3 masks the identity number and the contact value with recovery.ace_mask_value(...) inside the views. Architecture v5 gives the masking policy to P4 rwb-access and says masking is applied by rwb-source-data, but no source states which schema holds the function once the 19 schemas exist, or which service keeps the policy rows used for party data.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 line 2882 (P4 owns Recovery roles as data, scope, masking policy); slide 14 line 1043 (schema rwb_access: masking policy); slide 46 line 3064 (masking is applied by rwb-source-data); v3 Party fields rows 17, 18 and 35 (recovery.ace_mask_value).
proposed: Keep the function in the recovery view schema with the views, keep the policy rows in rwb_access (P4), and state in the P1 and P4 CON stories that rwb-source-data applies the mask in the view and in its responses.

title: The label Workbench no longer identifies an owner in a 19-service design
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Party and Customer Master Data Design v3.xlsx
section: Party fields (Source column, 25 rows); Match rules (row 9)
description: The Source column says Workbench for case_party, party_ext, contact_point_ext and partner, and M5 says the partner master is 'in the Workbench'. With 19 services 'Workbench' names no owner, so the source label cannot be resolved without the new Target schema column, which splits the same label across P3, P1 and S9.
evidence: v3 Party fields rows 5 to 10, 24 to 30, 45 to 51 and 52 to 58; v3 Match rules row 9; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 line 2880 to 2898 (the 19 services and their schemas); Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables rows case_party, party_ext, contact_point_ext and partner.
proposed: Keep the Source column as the origin of the data and read 'Workbench' as the owning service named in the Target schema column of the same row.

title: The statement 'there is no local party or contact_point table' conflicts with the two extension tables
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Party and Customer Master Data Design v3.xlsx
section: Party fields (row 5, design note) and the party_ext and contact_point_ext rows
description: The design note says a party is an ACE customer read through a view plus one party_ext row and that there is no local party or contact_point table, while the same sheet gives contact_point_ext seven local fields and makes party_ext a local table. A reader can take the note as forbidding both extension tables.
evidence: v3 Party fields row 5 (design note), rows 24 to 30 (party_ext) and rows 45 to 51 (contact_point_ext); Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables (party_ext P1, contact_point_ext P1); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 line 2884 (P1 owns the extension tables).
proposed: Read the note as 'there is no party master and no contact-point master'; the two extension tables stay with P1 and carry only the Workbench-only attributes.
